title: Circle Theorems: Angles in a Circle
seo_title: Circle Theorems – SSS 2 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Use the angle properties of circles: angle at the centre, angles in the same segment, angle in a semicircle and cyclic quadrilaterals. (summary of the NERDC SSS 2 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 2 maths worksheets on circle theorems: angle at the centre, same segment, semicircle and cyclic quadrilaterals. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Angle at the centre = 2 × angle at the circumference
key_sub: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180°.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc.
  • Angles in the same segment are equal; the angle in a semicircle is 90°.
  • Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°.

Examples

Example

Angle at the circumference = 35°

2 × 35°

Answer: Angle at the centre = 70°

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Halving instead of doublingThe centre angle is the bigger one.
Using the wrong arcBoth angles must stand on the same arc.
Calling any quadrilateral cyclicAll four vertices must be on the circle.

items.q: O is the centre of the circle. ∠AOB = 144° and P is on the minor arc AB. Find ∠APB.
items.e: P is on the minor arc, so use the reflex angle at the centre: 360° − 144° = 216°. ∠APB = 216° ÷ 2 = 108°.

items.q: ∠AOB = 90°. Find the measure of minor arc AB.

items.q: ∠AOB = 120°. Find the measure of the major arc from A to B (the long way around).

items.q: ∠AOB = (2x + 12)° and minor arc AB = 48°. Find x.
